 According to NBA insider Jake Fischer, Dillingham is signing a new deal to join the Westchester Knicks.
 Dillingham must first clear waivers. No NBA team should pick him up before he can finalize his move to the G League.
 Rob Dillingham signing deal to join G League's Westchester Knicks
 Rob Dillingham entered free agency after the Charlotte Hornets waived him last September as part of the team's roster-trimming move.
 The No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Dillingham spent his first two seasons with the Minnesota Timberwolves. He was traded to the Chicago Bulls at the 2025-26 trade deadline along with Leonard Miller and four second-round picks for Ayo Dosunmu and Julian Phillips.
 Dillingham was sent by the Bulls to the Hornets in exchange for Buddy Hield this past offseason, but he was subsequently released.
 He tallied 6.3 points, 2.2 assists, and 2.0 rebounds in 65 games split between Minnesota and Chicago last season before undergoing surgery in April to remove a ganglion cyst from his right wrist.
 Dillingham will now look to find his way back to the NBA after making the bold choice to go to the G League and join the New York Knicks' developmental team.
